QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_43

question.text: Under Regulation 20, the Investment Manager is prohibited from providing advisory services for investment in securities of investee companies where the AIF managed by it invests. What is the EXCEPTION to this prohibition?

answer.text: Advisory may be provided to investors of a Co-investment scheme or clients of a Co-investment Portfolio Manager (per PMS Regulations 2020).
No exception; the prohibition is absolute.
Advisory may be provided to any LP of the AIF on a reciprocal basis.
Advisory may be provided if the Manager obtains 51% LP consent.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Regulation 20(8): 'The Investment Manager shall not provide advisory services to any investor OTHER THAN the investors of a Co-investment scheme or clients of Co-investment Portfolio Manager as specified in the SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2020, for investment in securities of investee companies where the AIF managed by it makes an investment.' The Trap: Absolute prohibition (Option B) is wrong — co-investment exception exists. Reciprocal (Option C) and 51% LP consent (Option D) are invented workarounds. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers this. XXI-B (Portfolio Managers) exam drills the Co-investment Portfolio Manager variant. XIX-A distributor exam may test the LP-pitch angle (how Co-invest is offered). Manager's Pro-Tip: Register a Co-investment PMS arm if you want to offer deal-by-deal co-investments to select LPs without pro-rata restrictions. This is a common Cat I/II structure post-2020 amendments.
